referents.why: 'his heart' possessor is Pharaoh, the subject of the sentence (the one who sees and hardens).
'them' (third masculine plural) is Moses and Aaron, the pair who spoke to Pharaoh in Exo.8.8 and whom he would not listen to.
referents.category: object pronoun for a named pair

referents.why: 'he would not listen' (qatal, third masculine singular) in narrative; the subject of the sentence is Pharaoh.

links.why: 'saw that relief had come': the clause is what was seen, the object of the verb of seeing.
cl1 is the object of cl0 (what he saw), not a later event. The that link already carries it.
A separate waw before the infinitive absolute. The sequence is marked; the text gives time, not cause.
The hardening brings about the refusal. A plain 'and' is not a cause or result, and R4 gives 'a will hardened, then the refusal that follows' as result.
'he hardened his heart' and then 'would not listen': a will hardened, then the refusal that follows (R4).
'just as the LORD had said' is a comparison with a saying; the refusal is declared the fulfilment of the LORD's earlier word.

cant_tell.what: whether seeing the relief causes the hardening (cl0 to cl2)
cant_tell.why: The Hebrew sets seeing and then hardening with a waw. The text gives time, not cause; 'when' in the English is the translator's choice.
